subject: Logic
title: Affirming the Consequent
description: A quick, practical guide to Affirming the Consequent.

hook.text: "If it's a dog, it has four legs. It has four legs. Therefore it's a dog." Tables have four legs too.

buildup.text: Affirming the consequent takes "if P then Q" and wrongly concludes P from Q.

discovery.text: The valid form is modus ponens: affirm P, conclude Q. Reversing it creates a formal fallacy.

twist.text: It fools people because the conclusion often sounds reasonable—dogs do have four legs, after all.

climax.text: Multiple causes can produce the same effect. Don't assume only one cause is possible.

quiz.question: What mistake does affirming the consequent make?
options: Concluding the cause from the effect
